_comment: [OPUS-4.8] PERF RATCHET — the committed best-ever FLOOR per deterministic metric (smaller is better).
This is the source-of-record ratchet, reviewed in diffs exactly like the conformance RATCHET counts
in .github/workflows/ci.yml. scripts/perf-gate.py FAILS CI when a metric exceeds floor*(1+threshold),
so a sub-threshold regression EVERY commit can no longer slow-drift unbounded (the boiling-frog bug
that the prev-only gate had). See scripts/perf-gate.py header for the full ratchet protocol:
- 'auto' metrics: integer-exact byte layout; the floor auto-ratchets DOWN on genuine improvement
(a push-to-main step re-commits this file with [skip ci]). They NEVER auto-raise.
- 'noise' metrics: wall-clock-derived (parse_ns_per_byte ~3% run-to-run); gated against the floor
with a wide noise band and only ratcheted DOWN on a SUSTAINED improvement (median of recent
points below floor), never to a one-off noise-low.
- RAISE a floor (deliberate regression, e.g. a wasm bundle bump from a new feature) ONLY explicitly:
edit this file in a reviewed PR, OR set PERF_GATE_ALLOW='metric' for that run (re-floors to current).
Floors seeded 2026-06-13 from origin/benchmark-data dev/bench/data.js (57 published points): the
byte metrics are dead-flat (store=92, dict=53, small=88); wasm grew 1518547->1579288 across the series
via accepted feature additions, so its floor is seeded at the latest ACCEPTED value (1579288) — future
growth beyond +2% must now be an EXPLICIT raise. parse floor = median of the recent published points.
[OPUS-4.8] (sq-perf) 2026-06-15: parse_ns_per_byte floor CORRECTED 4.895 -> 4.9721. The 4.895 seed was
a NOISE-LOW of the cluster, not its median: across all 80 published points min=3.854 max=5.435
median=4.9721, and 81% of points (65/80) sit ABOVE 4.895 — even the pre-regression parent commit
7f3bb639 published 4.9721 on CI, so 4.895 was never reproducibly achievable on the runner class. The
gate's +17% trip (4.895->5.743) was a runner-contention spike measured against this too-aggressive
floor (no published point ever exceeded the OLD band 5.482, confirming the trip was a fresh outlier,
not drift in the code). 4.9721 is the documented basis ('median of recent published points'); with
the +12% band that is 5.5688, which comfortably covers the series max (5.4346) while still failing a
real slowdown. A separate parse-path code fix (skip the redundant triple-term serial pass on plain
N-Triples that PR #91 added) lands alongside, lowering the true cost on every runner.

[OPUS-4.8] (sq-7d3dj.1) 2026-07-02: wasm_bundle_bytes floor RE-BASELINED DOWNWARD 1686907 -> 1399703
(-17.0%) — an OPTIMISATION win, not a feature bump. The new `release-wasm` cargo profile (root Cargo.toml)
size-optimises the COLD, run-once parse crates (spargebra/oxiri/oxttl at opt-level "z") and strips local
symbols (strip=symbols), while the HOT engine/core query-eval crates stay opt-level 3 — so the bundle
shrinks with no runtime-perf change (pure parser code, off every hot path). BOTH the gate (scripts/ci-
bench.sh) AND the shipped bundle (js build:wasm{,:lean} -> wasm-pack --profile release-wasm) now build
this profile, so the gate builds under the same cargo profile as the shipped bundle (it ratchets the raw
cargo-build .wasm, not the post-wasm-bindgen/wasm-opt npm artifact). Measured split on the aarch64 work box (lean,
no-features build, identical to ci-bench.sh): release 1699660 -> strip-only 1561759 (-8.1%) -> +opt-z
1399703 (-17.65% total). Floor set to the aarch64 work-box AFTER value 1399703 — this is a WORK-BOX
measurement, not the canonical x86_64 CI value (which cannot be produced here). It is a SAFE upper bound:
the historical arch relationship has aarch64 reading ABOVE x86_64 (old bundle 1687481 aarch64 vs 1686907
x86_64, +0.034%), so the x86_64 CI build is expected at-or-just-below 1399703 and passes the strict gate;
the +2% band (=1427697) covers any residual cross-arch codegen delta. On the next push to main the auto-
ratchet-down step re-floors this to the exact x86_64 CI value. threshold 0.02 + mode auto UNCHANGED.

[SONNET-4.6] (sq-7d3dj.20) 2026-07-07: feature_off_exact RE-PINNED 1404910 -> 1407500 (+2590 bytes, +0.184%). The LFTJ micro-opt in sparq-substrate/join.rs (PR #1716) changes Vec<usize> -> SmallVec<[usize;8]> in the Leapfrog struct; sparq-engine unconditionally enables sparq-substrate/join so this code is compiled into the WASM bundle even though join.rs is behind cfg(feature="join"). The SmallVec generic monomorphization carries additional inline-storage code paths that increase WASM code size. This is NOT accidental vectorization (the invariant the zero-delta gate exists to protect); the feature-OFF INVARIANT (bundle identical with vectorized ON vs OFF) is PRESERVED. 1407500 is the CI x86_64 runner measurement (run to be confirmed, artifact-exact-equality leg2). The ratchet floor (1399703) is UNCHANGED: 1407500 sits within its +2% band (top 1427697), so bench.yml stays green.

[OPUS-4.8] (sq-7d3dj.30.2 / PR #1733) 2026-07-07: BOTH wasm_bundle_bytes floor AND feature_off_exact RE-PINNED 1407500 -> 1439315 (+31815 bytes, +2.260% vs feature_off_exact; +2.83% vs the 1399703 ratchet floor). CAUSE: PR #1733 makes ORDER BY ... LIMIT k use an UNCONDITIONAL bounded top-k selection path (sparq-engine order-by eval) with a precomputed SortCell::Iri sort key; SortCell::Iri and the bounded-heap selection code are always-compiled (NOT feature-gated), so they link into the feature-OFF wasm bundle and grow it. This is NOT accidental vectorization (the invariant the zero-delta gate exists to protect) and the feature-OFF INVARIANT (bundle identical with vectorized ON vs OFF) is PRESERVED — only the absolute baseline moved. UNLIKE the prior five within-band re-pins, this +2.83% EXCEEDS the old floor's +2% band (top 1427697), so the ratchet floor itself is RAISED (a documented, reviewed size bump), not just feature_off_exact. TRADEOFF (proceed-and-document): accept the size-for-speed cost — bounded top-k turns ORDER BY+LIMIT from a full sort-then-truncate O(n log n) into an O(n log k) heap, a latency win that includes wasm/browser queries where the bundle ships. 1439315 is the CI x86_64 runner measurement (run 28854869618, artifact-exact-equality leg2 'Measure wasm bundle size'; the perf-gate 'run + track benchmarks' lane reads the same 1439315). threshold 0.02 + mode auto UNCHANGED — the +2% guard is RETAINED at the new floor, not widened. Canonical cross-crate wasm-size re-measure = bead sq-7d3dj.30.6.

[OPUS-4.8] (sq-v3nel / PR TBD) 2026-07-07: feature_off_exact RETIRED (field REMOVED from metrics.wasm_bundle_bytes below; history preserved in this _comment chain, NOT deleted). WHY: the static exact-byte pin was ORDER-DEPENDENT and could not converge under a busy merge queue — every PR touching always-compiled engine/core code changed the merged-tree bundle bytes, the correct pin value depended on merge ORDER, and armed PRs cycled BLOCKED (e.g. #1726: gate + artifact-exact-equality FAILURE) while serial re-pin commits (#1733/#1747/#1745, and the six re-pins recorded above on 2026-07-02..07) chased a moving target. REPLACEMENT: the vectorized-feature-off gate leg 2 is now a DYNAMIC same-run byte-identity check — it builds the feature-OFF wasm TWICE in one CI run (base/merge-base tree vs head/merged tree) and compares byte-for-byte. Identical toolchain + run => deterministic, no static pin, no order dependence. A PR that does not touch always-compiled code => identical bytes => auto-pass; a PR that DOES must DECLARE it by incrementing change_token in bench/feature-off-declaration.json (audit-visible, reviewed diff — see that file's _comment). The INTENT of the old gate (catch ACCIDENTAL default-path/feature-off changes) is PRESERVED; the SIZE of an accepted change is still governed, UNCHANGED, by the metrics.wasm_bundle_bytes floor ratchet (+/-2% band) below and in bench.yml — that ratchet is NOT touched by this change. Implementation: scripts/check-vectorized-feature-off.py --leg2-dynamic + .github/workflows/vectorized-feature-off.yml artifact-exact-equality job (name kept: the only required check is ci-summary's `gate`; artifact-exact-equality is picked up by the aggregator by name, so the name is preserved).

[SONNET-4.6] (sq-7d3dj.32.2.5) 2026-07-10: comp_store_bytes_per_triple SEEDED 56. First-class deterministic ratchet for the COMPRESSED in-RAM store profile (SPARQ_STORE_PROFILE=compressed, i.e. Graph::into_compressed — block-compressed permutation indexes, SPQCPRM2 V2 format post-PR #1824). Floor measured by running the IDENTICAL ci-bench.sh stanza (SPARQ_STORE_PROFILE=compressed bench on the deterministic 200k-triple synthetic corpus, 3 consecutive runs all reading 56 B/triple — integer-exact, runner-noise-immune). A deliberate raise (e.g. a new perm or a format feature that widens block headers) MUST come via a reviewed PR or PERF_GATE_ALLOW, matching the existing wasm_bundle_bytes raise protocol.
